---
title: Get started
---

Building a time-series model means the same steps every time, and much of
the effort goes into turning their output into a document. `dazflow` runs
the steps from configuration and renders every result in one house style.
This page follows one project, the example that `dazflow init` writes,
through the main ideas. Every output below is pasted from a real run.

```sh
pip install dazflow
dazflow init loss-rate
```

```
created loss-rate (11 files); next: dazflow validate -p loss-rate
```

The folder holds `project.yaml`, one file per step under `config/` with
every setting written out at its default, and example data under
`data/raw/`: a quarterly loss rate, two drivers (GDP growth and
unemployment) and three scenarios for them.

## Run the pipeline

```python
import dazflow as dz

project = dz.project.load("loss-rate")
run = project.run()
run.passed, run.steps
```

```
(True, ('ingest', 'clean', 'explore', 'build', 'select', 'forecast', 'diagnose', 'report'))
```

`project.run()` runs every step in memory and writes nothing. Each step's
result is in `run.results`, by step name.

## Gates and findings

Every step ends in a gate: checks of its numbers against thresholds set
in configuration. Explore's checks that each driver has its expected sign
and is significant:

```python
ex = run.results["explore"]
ex.gate.passed, [c.name for c in ex.gate.checks]
```

```
(True, ['sign:gdp_growth', 'significance:gdp_growth', 'sign:unemployment', 'significance:unemployment'])
```

A finding is a sentence from a template, filled with the step's numbers;
`dz.render.finding_text` writes them in the house style, as the reports
and the command line do (`ex.finding.text` keeps them as computed):

```python
print(dz.render.finding_text(ex.finding))
```

```
3 series explored; 2 were differenced to stationarity. 2 of 2 drivers are kept, 0 of them by override: each has its expected sign and a p-value of at most 0.05.
```

A failed check is reported, never hidden, and is accepted only with a
reason written in configuration. The example's RESET test fails, and
`config/diagnose.yaml` overrides it:

```python
check = run.results["diagnose"].gate["reset"]
check.status, round(check.observed, 3), check.threshold
```

```
('overridden', 0.027, 0.05)
```

```python
print(check.override.reason)
```

```
Example data: RESET rejects the linear form at 5% (p = 0.03). The series were made up for the example; a real model would revisit its functional form before use.
```

## Tables and figures

Tables and figures carry stable identifiers, `T<step>.<n>` and
`F<step>.<n>`, that survive reruns, so a document can cite them.

```python
sorted(ex.artefacts)
```

```
['F3.1', 'S3.1', 'T3.1', 'T3.2', 'T3.3', 'T3.4']
```

```python
print(dz.render.render(ex.artefacts["T3.3"], "markdown"))
```

```
Table T3.3. Driver screen

| Driver | Lag | Correlation | Coefficient | Standard error (HAC) | t | p-value | Observations | Expected sign | Observed sign | Result |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| gdp\_growth | 0 | -0.84 | -0.15 | 0.01 | -18.95 | 0.00 | 119 | negative | negative | Pass |
| unemployment | 0 | 0.90 | 0.39 | 0.02 | 21.49 | 0.00 | 119 | positive | positive | Pass |

Each driver is regressed alone on the transformed target at the lag of strongest correlation (0 to 4); it is kept with its expected sign and a p-value of at most 0.05.
```

The same table renders to `html` and `docx`, and figures to `svg` and
`png`, through `dz.render.render` and `dz.render.write`.

## One step at a time

Each step is also one call that takes a dataset and its configuration. A
later step takes an earlier one's result as an argument rather than
importing it, so any step can run on its own:

```python
ds = run.results["clean"].dataset
ds.targets, ds.drivers
```

```
(('loss_rate',), ('gdp_growth', 'unemployment'))
```

```python
again = dz.explore.run(ds, project.step_config("explore"))
again.finding.text == ex.finding.text
```

```
True
```

Select scores every candidate out of sample and proposes one; the proposal
stands until it is confirmed in `config/select.yaml`:

```python
sel = run.results["select"]
sel.chosen, sel.decision
```

```
('ols:gdp_growth+unemployment', 'proposed')
```

## Write, report and replay

`project.write(run)` writes the datasets, every step's tables, figures and
finding under `reports/<step>/`, the Word document, and the run record.

```python
record = project.write(run)
record.run.status, sorted(p.name for p in (project.root / "reports").iterdir())
```

```
('passed', ['build', 'clean', 'diagnose', 'document', 'explore', 'forecast', 'ingest', 'record.json', 'report', 'select'])
```

```python
sorted(p.name for p in (project.root / "reports" / "document").iterdir())
```

```
['document.docx', 'replay.py']
```

The document is built from the run record alone: a contents list, a
summary, one section per step in pipeline order and the configuration in
an appendix. A replay reruns every step from the record and compares every
recorded number with what it computes now, floats within a relative 1e-9
and everything else exactly:

```python
replay = project.replay()
replay.passed, replay.differences
```

```
(True, ())
```

## Score any form

Any model form, built in or not, can be scored out of sample by refitting
it at successive origins:

```python
y = ds.frame["loss_rate"]
X = ds.frame[["gdp_growth", "unemployment"]]
ev = dz.evaluation.evaluate(
    dz.models.get("ols")(), y, X,
    splitter=dz.evaluation.Expanding(initial=80, horizon=4),
)
round(ev.score("rmse"), 3), round(ev.score("coverage"), 3)
```

```
(0.077, 0.919)
```

That is the root mean squared error over the four horizons, and the share
of actual values inside the 95% interval.
